maps.name: The North Reach
maps.description: The cold country between Hollowmere's dark woods and Varnfell's empty harbor — one road, two towns, and a great deal of ground that has recently stopped being quiet underneath.

maps.name: Hollowmere
maps.description: The last village on the dragon's road. Slate roofs, shuttered windows, a chapel bell that still rings the dusk. Hollowmere has stood here since before the Auric Throne fell, and most of its folk would rather die in their gardens than be driven out by a wyrm.

maps.name: Mira Hask's Provisions
maps.description: Hollowmere's general store — torches, lockpicks, healing herbs, and whatever Mira talked the last caravan out of before it turned back south. The shelves are thinner every week the dragon stays in the sky.

maps.name: Orin's Forge
maps.description: Orin the Smith's crossroads forge, smoke rising day and night. The anvil is old campaign steel; the prices are honest; the smith's left hand is missing two fingers and the goblin who took them is dead.

maps.name: Varnfell
maps.description: A fur-and-ore trading post at the cold edge of the map, where the snow meets a grey sea. The ships stopped coming two seasons ago, the tradeway south runs thick with wolves, and the old delve below the ridge has started breathing warm air. The Varnfell folk stay anyway. Somebody has to keep the lamps lit this far north.

maps.name: Varn & Daughters Trading Post
maps.description: Three generations of Varns have weighed furs and brimite ore across this counter. The shelves are still full — that's the problem. Nothing has shipped south since the wolves took the tradeway.

maps.name: The Driftwood Hearth
maps.description: Varnfell's only inn, built from the timbers of a ship that wrecked on the sand the year the post was founded. The fire never goes out. Doran Pike sees to that personally.

maps.name: Thornbury
maps.description: A small market town on the Greymantle road — one inn, one shop, and everybody knowing everybody's business.

maps.name: The Gilded Goose
maps.description: Thornbury's only inn — warm hearth, long memory.

maps.name: Thornbury General Goods
maps.description: Sundries, tools, and gossip at fair prices.

maps.name: Thornbury Cottage
maps.description: A modest cottage off the market square.

maps.name: Elderbough
maps.description: A clearing-town grown up around a druid treaty-sapling, deep in the North Reach forest. The houses are timbered with deadfall only — not one living tree has ever been cut inside the bounds, and the town means to keep it that way.

maps.name: The Moot Hall
maps.description: Elderbough's inn, court, and council chamber in one timbered room. Disputes are settled by show of hands; rounds are settled by Petra.

maps.name: Tansy's Stillroom
maps.description: Drying racks, salve pots, and a counter worn smooth by three generations of Mosswane hands. It smells of every season at once.

maps.name: The Heartwood Grove
maps.description: The treaty-sapling, eleven generations grown, and the spring it drinks from. Iron stays sheathed here, salt is shared, and no flame has ever been struck inside the tree-ring.

maps.name: Lastlight
maps.description: The last town before the cracks, walled in dark stone and lit at all hours — the lamps are doctrine here, not decoration. Below the north stair, the ground is open where it shouldn't be, and the town's whole purpose is standing in the way.

maps.name: The Last Lamp
maps.description: Lastlight's inn, named for the lamp over its door that has never been allowed to go out. The watch drinks here in shifts, the scholar in the corner pays for his room in warnings, and nobody sits with their back to the north window.

maps.name: Chapel of the Vigil
maps.description: Every name in the watch-yard is read aloud here nightly, oldest first. The Vigil holds that the dead stay down so long as they are remembered correctly — and that the things below are counting on the town to forget.

maps.name: The Near Crack
maps.description: A scar in the earth a hundred paces from Lastlight's wall, breathing warm air and counting-quiet. The watch keeps a warding line of standing stones between the crack and the town, and replaces the stones more often than it talks about.

maps.name: The Royal Armory
maps.description: A hidden cache of relics and ancient weapons

maps.name: Castle Eastmarch
maps.description: The walled seat of the Eastmarch — four towers, one gate, and a garrison stretched thin.

maps.name: Eastmarch Great Hall
maps.description: Banner-hung hall of the Eastmarch lords, colder than it looks.

maps.name: Eastmarch Keep, Upper Floor
maps.description: The lord's solar and the castle's strongbox — guests are rarely invited this far.

maps.name: Mournfield
maps.description: The old burial ground at the swamp's edge. The rows are neat, the gate is iron, and the ground has started keeping its own hours.

maps.name: Mournfield Crypt
maps.description: Family vaults stacked four deep. Several lids are no longer where the masons left them.

maps.name: Mournfield Deep Crypt
maps.description: The oldest level, pre-dating the town above it. The altar here was not built for any god the chapel recognises.

maps.name: The Umbral Spire, Ground Floor
maps.description: A black-brick tower alone in the pines. The lights in the upper windows do not match any honest fire.

maps.name: The Umbral Spire, Library Floor
maps.description: Shelves of things that read back. The dust here settles in patterns.

maps.name: The Umbral Spire, Sanctum
maps.description: The mage's working room. The circle on the floor is cold — for now.

maps.name: Fire Shrine — Ashen Antechamber
maps.description: A shrine cut into the volcanic range. The braziers were burning when the first explorers arrived; nobody lit them.

maps.name: Fire Shrine — Hall of Embers
maps.description: A molten channel crosses the hall, spanned by one scorched bridge. The heat has opinions.

maps.name: Fire Shrine — Magma Vault
maps.description: The deepest chamber, where the shrine keeps what the fire was built to honour — or contain.
